analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including deletion and mode metadata. bedrock-smoke.yml:9 changes runner hosting; its master-only dispatch gate, immutable checkout, hash-required dependencies, bounded runtime and OIDC permission remain unchanged (8–38). No evidence establishes a runner-specific security prerequisite invalidated by this move.
ci-dev.yml:18,29–34,37–72 makes PR tests label-triggered, coalesces dev pushes, adds a separate label-removal job with write permissions, and forwards cluster_gpu. The removal script uses quoted environment variables and does not check out PR code. Deleting ci-dev-hourly.yml:1–38 and ci-dev.yml base:60–99 removes periodic full testing and failure notifications, but supplied evidence does not establish these as mandatory release/qualification controls. No supported serving-authorization, encryption, billing or cache-isolation regression follows directly (A-017, T-054, T-041).
Only test-threat-model-review.py:731–737 changes: assertions now expect label opt-in and GitHub-hosted runners. Surrounding tests cover stale snapshots, incomplete retries, redaction and trusted scanner checkout, but assertions are not proof of the actual workflow behavior.
Integration must inspect threat-model-review.yml and the remaining ci-master.yml source (only metadata and a bounded orientation patch supplied here), then reconcile label-triggered execution with provider-plan.yml/provider-tests.yml tested-tree deduplication and qualification requirements. Confirm opt-in or cancelled runs cannot become reusable successful test evidence, and that secret-bearing scanning still executes only trusted code. These contracts are outside this supplied source scope; no vulnerability is inferred from their absence.
